title: Noah, the Ark and the Rainbow
bigQuestion: What does the Torah say a promise is, and how did Noah's family learn about one?

story.title: A Leaf in Her Beak
story.kicker: After many days of rain and waiting, a small bird flies home with big news.
paragraphs: Rain, rain, rain. In the Torah's story, Noah's family sat inside a very big boat. The boat was full of animals. Sheep bleated. Doves cooed. Lions yawned. Outside, water covered everything. There was no land to see.
One day the rain stopped. Noah opened a window. He let a dove fly out. The dove flew and flew. She found no place to land. She came back tired. Noah put out his hand and took her in.

Seven days later, Noah sent the dove out again. Everyone waited. Then, near evening, a small shape came through the sky. It was the dove. In her beak was a fresh green leaf. An olive leaf! Somewhere, a tree was growing.

Everyone on the boat cheered. The water was going down. Soon they would walk on dry land again. The Torah's story says the dove went out one more time. That time, she did not come back. She had found a home.
story.think: Why did everyone cheer when they saw the leaf? What did the leaf tell them?

lessons.title: Noah Builds an Ark
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah says God told Noah to build a very big boat called an ark.
reading: The Torah tells about a man named *Noah*. The story says the world was full of bad ways. But Noah was good. The Torah says God told Noah that a big flood was coming.
God told Noah to build an *ark*. An ark is a very big boat. Noah made it from wood. He covered it inside and out so water could not get in. It had a door on the side and a window on top.
The ark had three floors. It was very long. It took Noah a long time to build. His three sons helped. Their names were Shem, Ham and Japheth.

words.d: the man in the Torah who built the ark
the very big boat that Noah built in the Torah's story

look.title: How Big Was the Ark?
look.prompt: Which number is the biggest? Was the ark longer or taller?

check.q: What is an ark?
check.why: In the Torah's story, the ark is the very big boat Noah built.

check.q: Why does the Torah say Noah built the ark?
check.why: The story says God told Noah a flood was coming, so Noah built the ark.

check.q: How many floors did the ark have, in the story?
check.why: The Torah says the ark had three floors: a bottom, a middle and a top.

lessons.title: Two by Two
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah says the animals came into the ark two by two.
reading: The story says the animals came to the ark. They came in *pairs*. A pair is two. One boy and one girl of each kind. Birds, cows, snakes, bugs. Some kinds came in bigger groups of seven pairs.
Noah's family went in too. Noah, his wife, his three sons and their wives. That is eight people. Then, the story says, God closed the door.
Picture the line of animals. Two giraffes with long necks. Two mice with tiny feet. Two elephants stomping up the ramp. That is how many children picture it.

words.d: two of something that go together

look.title: Line Up the Animals
look.text: Look at the line going up the ramp. Two ducks waddle. Two horses trot. Two turtles go very, very slowly. Behind them, two frogs hop. The Torah's story says they came two by two, a boy and a girl of each kind.
look.prompt: Pick an animal. Say its name two times, one for each in the pair.

check.q: How does the Torah say the animals came into the ark?
check.why: The story says the animals came two by two, a pair of each kind.

check.q: What is a pair?
check.why: A pair is two things that go together, like two shoes.

check.q: How many people does the Torah say went into the ark?
check.why: Noah, his wife, his three sons and their wives make eight people.

lessons.title: Forty Days of Rain
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah says it rained for forty days and forty nights.
reading: The Torah says the rain began. It rained for *forty* days and forty nights. Forty is a lot of days. It is more than a month. Water covered the land. Water covered even the hills.
The ark floated on top of the water. Inside, Noah's family fed the animals. They waited. The Torah says God remembered Noah. Then a wind blew, and the water started to go down.
The ark came to rest on a mountain. The mountains of Ararat, the Torah says. But the water was still high. Noah had to wait some more.

words.d: the number 40; the Torah says the rain lasted forty days and forty nights

look.title: Counting the Days
rows: Days Noah waited before sending the dove again
Times the dove was sent out
look.cite: Genesis (Bereshit) 7:12 and 8:8–12, Jewish Publication Society translation, 1917
look.prompt: Which number is the biggest? Which is the smallest?

check.q: How long does the Torah say it rained?
check.why: The Torah says it rained forty days and forty nights.

check.q: What is a flood?
check.why: A flood is water that covers the land. In the story, it covered the hills.

check.q: Where does the Torah say the ark came to rest?
check.why: The Torah says the ark rested on the mountains of Ararat.

lessons.title: The Dove and the Leaf
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah says a dove brought back an olive leaf, a sign that the water was going down.
reading: Noah wanted to know if the land was dry. He sent out a raven first. Then he sent a *dove*. A dove is a soft gray or white bird. The first time, the dove found no place to land. She came back.
Noah waited seven days. He sent the dove again. This time she came back with an *olive leaf* in her beak. Now Noah knew. Trees were growing. The water was going down.
Seven more days. Noah sent the dove one more time. She did not come back. Then Noah opened the ark, and the story says God told the family to come out.

words.d: a soft gray or white bird; in the Torah's story it brought Noah an olive leaf
a small green leaf from an olive tree; a sign that land was near

look.title: The Dove Comes Home
look.text: The Torah says the dove came back to Noah in the evening. In her mouth was an olive leaf, freshly picked. So Noah knew that the water had gone down from the earth.
look.cite: Genesis (Bereshit) 8:11, paraphrased from the Jewish Publication Society translation, 1917
look.prompt: How did the leaf tell Noah the water was going down?

check.q: What did the dove bring back?
check.why: The dove brought back an olive leaf. It was a sign that trees were growing.

check.q: Which bird did Noah send out first?
check.why: The Torah says Noah sent a raven first, then the dove.

check.q: What did the leaf tell Noah?
check.why: A leaf means a tree was growing on dry ground. The water was going down.

lessons.title: The Rainbow Promise
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah says the rainbow is a sign of God's promise never to flood the whole world again.
reading: When the ground was dry, everyone came out of the ark. The animals ran and flew. The Torah says Noah said thank you to God. Then God made a *promise*. God said there would never again be a flood over all the earth.
The story says God put a *rainbow* in the clouds. The rainbow is a sign. It is like a reminder. When people see a rainbow, they can remember the promise.
Jewish tradition has a blessing for seeing a rainbow. It thanks God for remembering the promise. A promise is something you say you will do. And then you do it.

words.d: something you say you will do, and then you do it
the bow of colors in the sky; the Torah says it is a sign of God's promise

look.title: A Bow in the Cloud
look.text: The Torah says God set a bow in the cloud. It would be a sign of the promise between God and the earth.
look.cite: Genesis (Bereshit) 9:13, paraphrased from the Jewish Publication Society translation, 1917
look.prompt: What is the rainbow a sign of, in the story?

check.q: What does the Torah say the rainbow is?
check.why: The story says the rainbow is a sign of God's promise never to flood the whole earth again.

check.q: What is a promise?
choices: Something you say you will do, and then do
check.why: A promise is a thing you say you will do. Keeping it means doing it.

check.q: What does Jewish tradition say when someone sees a rainbow?
choices: A blessing that remembers the promise
check.why: Jewish tradition has a blessing for a rainbow. It remembers God's promise.

lessons.title: The Tower of Babel
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah says people built a tall tower, and then they began to speak many languages.
reading: After the flood, the Torah says, everyone spoke one *language*. A language is the words people use to talk. The people came to a flat land. They said, "Let us build a city and a tower up to the sky."
They made bricks. They built and built. The story says God came down to see the tower. Then God mixed up their words. They could not understand each other. They stopped building.
The people spread out over the earth. The place was called *Babel*. Jewish tradition reads this story as a lesson. Some rabbis say the people cared more about the tower than about each other.

words.d: the words people use to talk to each other
the place in the Torah where people built a tower and began to speak many languages

look.title: Who Can Understand?
look.text: Picture a big building site. One worker says, "Pass me a brick," in one language. The next worker hears sounds she does not know. She hands him a jug of water instead. Nobody can plan together anymore.
look.prompt: What happens to a big job when people cannot understand each other?

check.q: What did the people at Babel try to build?
choices: A tower up to the sky
check.why: The Torah says the people tried to build a city and a tower up to the sky.

check.q: What is a language?
choices: The words people use to talk
check.why: A language is the set of words people use to talk to each other.

check.q: Why did the people stop building, in the story?
choices: They could not understand each other
check.why: The Torah says their words were mixed up. They could not understand each other.

lessons.title: One Story, Many Families
lessons.mainIdea: Jews, Christians and Muslims all tell a story of Noah, and each reads it in its own way.
reading: Noah's story is in the Torah. Jewish families read it in the synagogue every fall. *Christians* read the same story in their Bible. Many Christian churches in Chicago tell it to children too.
*Muslims* tell a story of Noah too. In Arabic, his name is Nuh. The Qur'an, the holy book of Islam, has a chapter named after him. It tells how Nuh warned people and built a boat.
Each tradition reads the story in its own way. But all three tell of a good man, a big boat and a promise. You may hear it in a synagogue, a church or a mosque.

words.d: people who follow Christianity; they read Noah's story in their Bible
people who follow Islam; their holy book, the Qur'an, tells of Noah, called Nuh

check.why: Christians read Noah's story in their Bible, and many churches tell it to children.

review.q: What did Noah build, in the Torah's story?
review.why: Noah built an ark, a very big boat, because a flood was coming.

review.q: How did the animals come into the ark?
review.why: The Torah says the animals came two by two, a pair of each kind.

review.q: How many days did it rain?
review.why: The Torah says it rained for forty days and forty nights.

review.q: What did the dove bring back to the ark?
review.why: The dove brought an olive leaf. It showed the water was going down.

review.q: What does the Torah say the rainbow means?
choices: A promise: no more flood over all the earth
review.why: The Torah says the rainbow is a sign of God's promise never to flood the whole earth again.

review.q: What happened at Babel, in the story?
choices: People began to speak many languages
review.why: At Babel, the Torah says, the people's words were mixed up into many languages.
